title: Annotatio III §.I: Definition — one substance into another under residual accidents; ORTUS / PROGRESSUS plan
pass_a_gloss: For just as Transmutation of any thing whatever is a transformation of either exterior or interior form, so Transsubstantiation of precisely one substance into another (the accidents of the former, exposed to the senses, remaining, but those of the latter, into which the passage is made, absorbed and at least not obvious to any sense) signifies a mutation by an utterly unheard-of example. About to hand down its History here in a compendium, only because of kinship with Consubstantiation, we shall set two parts of the Tractation as it were: the Prior will probe the ORTUS of Transsubstantiation in its causes; the Posterior will make conspicuous its PROGRESSUS in modes and degrees.
pass_b_english: Transmutation reshapes form; Transsubstantiation turns one substance into another while sense-exposed accidents of the former remain and those of the latter are absorbed — a mutation without precedent.
Plan: ORTUS (causes) then PROGRESSUS (modes and degrees), treated here only for kinship with Consubstantiation.
source_text: Quemadmodum enim Transmutatio rei cujuscunque, transformatio vel exterioris, vel interioris formæ; sic Transsubstantiatio unius præcisè substantiæ in aliam (remanentibus sensibusque expositis prioris, seu transmutandæ, posterioris verò, seu in quam transitio fit, absorptis, nulli saltem sensui obviis Accidentibus) mutationem inaudito prorsus exemplo significat. Hujus Historiam, ob cognationem solùm cum Consubstantiatione, hoc locô, per compendium, tradituri, duas quasi Tractationis partes, constituemus, quarum Prior ORTUM Transsubstantiationis in caussis suis rimabitur: Posterior PROGRESSUM ejusdem in modis gradibusque conspicuum reddet.

lemmas.gloss: of precisely one substance into another
